items.title: Forum des territoires du 9 au 12 juin à Bruxelles : le carrefour des acteurs euro-africains du développement local
items.description: Bruxelles est le point de convergence des acteurs européens et africains du développement territorial, depuis deux ans. À l’origine de cette dynamique, le Forum des territoires : une plateforme économique et diplomatique qui réunit élus, entrepreneurs, experts, investisseurs, responsables institutionnels et diaspora. Du 9 au 12 juin 2027, la capitale européenne accueillera la troisième édition ; un moment de rencontre au service du développement local. Depuis deux ans, différents acteurs africains et européens du développement local se retrouvent à Bruxelles, dans le cadre du Forum des territoires. Rien que pour la deuxième édition, explique une note, 378 participants ont été enregistrés, dont 15 nationalités, 200 membres de la diaspora, 180 entreprises, 480 rencontres d’affaires, 30 intentions de partenariats, 10 projets territoriaux présentés et plusieurs centaines de millions d’euros en opportunités d’affaires identifiées. Pour M. Senan Orphée A. Kinss, initiateur et coordonnateur du Forum des territoires, « dans un monde marqué par les bouleversements climatiques, les reconfigurations géoéconomiques, les transitions démographiques et les révolutions technologiques, une évidence s’impose progressivement : les modèles de développement exclusivement pensés depuis les centres de décision montrent aujourd’hui leurs limites ». Poursuivant, il a avoué que les réponses aux grands défis contemporains prennent désormais racine « là où vivent les populations, là où s’expriment les initiatives, là où se créent les richesses : dans nos communes, nos régions, nos terroirs ». C’est pourquoi, le forum des territoires, a rappelé Souleymane Amar, ingénieur en développement et marketing territorial, président du comité scientifique, est « un espace de confiance où se croisent élus, experts, entrepreneurs, investisseurs, institutions et membres de la diaspora, tous acteurs d’un monde en mouvement, où les territoires sont les moteurs du développement ». Les deux premières éditions qui ont, selon lui, enregistré « des résultats concrets » et posé les bases d’une dynamique durable avec les expériences de plusieurs collectivités sénégalaises dont Vélingara et Notto Diobass, en donnent une illustration. Pour cette dernière collectivité territoriale, souligne M. Amar, « la participation à la deuxième édition du forum, organisée à Bruxelles du 3 au 6 juin dernier, a constitué une opportunité de renforcer son positionnement et de poursuivre la mobilisation de partenaires autour de ses ambitions de développement ». Des résultats enregistrés Parmi les acquis de Notto Diobass figure notamment « la consolidation du partenariat avec le groupe Sablux, acteur du secteur immobilier. Cette relation ouvre des perspectives autour de l’aménagement territorial, du développement urbain et de la promotion de nouveaux modèles d’habitat », a dit M. Amar. À ce titre, les autorités municipales ont également, poursuit le président du comité scientifique, pu échanger avec plusieurs partenaires économiques et collectivités territoriales belges et européennes. Le Conseil départemental de Vélingara a aussi, avec le Forum, élargi ses perspectives de coopération et à renforcer son ouverture sur les partenaires internationaux. La collectivité territoriale « a notamment noué une relation de partenariat avec une structure canadienne, tout en développant des échanges avec plusieurs villes belges », informe M. Amar. Ces ouvertures, note-t-il, illustrent le potentiel de la coopération territoriale lorsqu’elle permet de mettre directement en relation des collectivités partageant des préoccupations ou des ambitions communes. Les expériences de Notto Diobass et de Vélingara, auxquelles s’ajoutent les collaborations économiques nouées entre partenaires privés, permettent de mieux comprendre la valeur ajoutée du Forum des territoires, a assuré son responsable du comité scientifique. Un échange avec une ville européenne, selon M. Amar, peut évoluer vers un partenariat de coopération décentralisée, des missions d’expertise ou des programmes de renforcement des capacités des agents municipaux. Capitaliser sur les acquis et aller plus loin Fortes de ces expériences, les collectivités locales de Notto Diobass et de Vélingara ont engagé leur participation à la troisième édition du Forum. Pour elles, « il ne s’agit plus seulement de découvrir une plateforme de coopération, mais de capitaliser sur les relations établies et de faire progresser les initiatives amorcées », a informé M. Amar. La troisième édition, prévue à Bruxelles du 9 au 12 juin 2027, sera une occasion de présenter des projets mieux documentés, de préciser les besoins d’accompagnement, de consolider les partenariats existants et d’élargir les réseaux de coopération. Les collectivités pourront notamment mieux cibler les partenaires susceptibles de les accompagner dans des domaines tels que l’aménagement urbain, les infrastructures, l’habitat, les services publics locaux, le développement économique et la transition écologique. Amadou Maguette NDAW

items.title: Military aircraft crashes, 19 dead
items.description: A military transport plane crashed on Tuesday in the Siberian region of Kemerovo, killing all 19 onboard, Russian media reported, citing a statement from Moscow’s defence ministry. “An An-12 military transport aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo Region while on a scheduled flight. The plane went down in an uninhabited area. There were 19 people on board, including the crew, they all perished,” the Russian defence ministry was quoted as saying by state news agency TASS. The preliminary cause of the crash is a technical malfunction, TASS added. “A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is working at the site to establish all the circumstances of the incident,” the ministry’s statement was quoted as saying by RIA Novosti. Kemerovo region’s governor, Ilya Seredyuk, said earlier on Telegram that there had been an “aviation incident” near the village of Yagunovo. He added that “an aircraft, which was in transit through our region, has presumably crashed”. Seredyuk posted a video from the site in which multiple fire engines and ambulances could be seen, their lights blaring in the dark. items.title: Benue Justice Commissioner resigns with immediate effect
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State, Prof. Timothy Ornguga, has resigned his appointment with immediate effect, barely one year and two months in office. The Attorney-General announced his decision in a resignation letter dated November 13, 2026, addressed to Governor Hyacinth Alia through the Secretary to the State Government, SSG. The letter, titled, “Resignation from the Appointment as Honourable Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Benue State,” formally communicated his decision to step down from the position with immediate effect. He disclosed that he had served the state for one year, two months and two weeks, expressing appreciation to Governor Alia for the confidence reposed in him and the opportunity to serve. The resignation letter, which bears an official receipt stamp dated November 16, 2026, stated: “I write with profound respect and deep sense of responsibility to formally tender my resignation from my appointment as the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State. The resignation is with immediate effect. Having had the privilege of serving in this esteemed capacity for the past one year, two months, and two weeks.” He further stated: “I consider it an honour to have been entrusted with the responsibility of serving our dear state and contributing in my own capacity to the administration of justice, the promotion of the rule of law and the advancement of good governance. I am sincerely grateful to Your Excellency for the confidence reposed in me and for the opportunity to serve.” Contacted, the Media of the former Justice Commissioner, Jude Ekpendu confirmed the development. Meanwhile, efforts to ascertain the circumstances surrounding his resignation were unsuccessful as the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said he was unaware of the development when contacted. items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : l’image du Sénégal progresse de 606 %
items.description: Les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026 ont offert une vitrine internationale au Sénégal. Selon les premières analyses présentées par le directeur de la communication des Jeux, Abdoulaye Kanouté, l’image du pays a enregistré une progression d’environ 606 % par rapport à la période précédant l’événement. « Les premières analyses font état d’une progression d’environ 606 % de l’image du Sénégal », a déclaré Abdoulaye Kanouté, dans un bilan relayé dans l’émission « Salimto » sur la Radiodiffusion télévision sénégalaise (RTS). Un résultat qui témoigne de la portée médiatique de cette première édition des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse organisée sur le continent africain. Cette visibilité s’est notamment traduite par un important intérêt des médias nationaux et internationaux. Au total, 1 800 demandes d’accréditation ont été enregistrées, dont 600 médias ont obtenu leur accréditation pour couvrir la compétition. Une mobilisation qui a contribué à porter l'actualité des JOJ et, au-delà, à faire connaître le Sénégal auprès d'un public international. Sur le plan organisationnel, le dispositif de communication et de gestion des risques a également été renforcé. Plus de 300 procédures de normalisation et de prévention (PNP) ont ainsi été mises en place afin d'anticiper les éventuels incidents et d'assurer une meilleure maîtrise des opérations. Au-delà des performances sportives et du succès organisationnel, ces premiers chiffres mettent en évidence les retombées médiatiques des JOJ Dakar 2026. Le rendez-vous olympique aura ainsi constitué une occasion majeure pour le Sénégal de renforcer son rayonnement et de consolider son image sur la scène internationale. Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.title: Former KP ministers Jhagra, Bangash among 3 PTI leaders held under MPO despite bail from PHC
items.description: PESHAWAR: Former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa ministers Taimoor Saleem Jhagra and Kamran Bangash were among three PTI leaders taken into “preventative” custody by police shortly after they were granted interim bail by the high court. Jhagra, Bangash and PTI’s Peshawar president Irfan Saleem had been granted bail until Nov 17 (today) by an anti-terrorism court (ATC) in the 2023 case pertaining to vandalism and arson at the Radio Pakistan building during the May 9 riots . Earlier in the day, an ATC denied the three leaders bail that had been extended twice previously, following which they evaded arrest to reach the Peshawar High Court (PHC). Chief Justice SM Attique Shah, heading the single-member bench, pronounced an order granting the three leaders bail till Nov 23, on the condition of furnishing two sureties of Rs1 million each or depositing cash equivalent to it. The judge directed them to join the investigation and appear before the investigating officer as and when required. Following the order, an hours-long standoff unfolded between a huge police force present around PHC and the three petitioners. Led by Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Operations Farhan Khan, the police aimed to take the PTI leaders into custody, stating that the district administration had issued detention orders under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance. The petitioners had taken refuge in the PHC’s barroom, where several members of Insaf Lawyers Forum (ILF) were also accompanying them. During ensuing developments, the SSP visited them in the barroom to negotiate their surrender. Finally, at around 6pm, the PTI leaders left the barroom and were taken into custody by the police at the high court’s entrance. They were detained under the MPO ordinance, SSP Farhan told media persons at the high court. PHC approached after ATC denies bail Jhagra, Bangash and Saleem were among those named in the supplementary charge-sheet submitted to the ATC last month, though they had later been allowed pre-arrest bail. Sohail Afridi, the non-functional chief minister, had also been added as an accused in the case. The court last week initiated proceedings to declare Afridi and activist Mohammad Amir Khan proclaimed offenders. While both of them have reportedly been in preventive custody, the police have claimed that they could not be traced in pursuance of their arrest warrants. On Tuesday, an ATC presided over by Judge Wali Muhammad Khan decided not to confirm pre-arrest bails of Jhagra, Bangash and Saleem. The three leaders appeared along with their counsel, while senior lawyer Shabbir Hussain Gigyani represented the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation (PBC). The petitioners’ lawyers challenged the veracity of video footage on the basis of which they had been nominated in the case, stating that it had not yet been clarified from where those videos were obtained and who had prepared them. They argued that the petitioners’ mere presence in the said videos was not proof of any crime, nor had they been seen vandalising property. Therefore, they argued that the allegations against them were baseless and pre-arrest bail be confirmed. Advocate Gigyani opposed the PTI leaders’ bails, arguing that the current PBC’s station director Tufail Ahmed was posted as a programme manager at the time of the incident, while Nadra and Punjab Forensic Science Agency had confirmed the identification of the suspects in the videos, after which police nominated them in the supplementary challan. He stated that videos of the suspects were still present on social media. The ATC rejected the PTI leaders’ applications. The situation turned tense when police tried to arrest the three leaders after the order’s pronouncement. While they briefly caught hold of Bangash and Saleem, ILF members managed to free them from police custody. Later, police closed all entry and exit routes to the Judicial Complex, upon which lawyers forced their way to the adjoining PHC building, where the three PTI leaders also reached. In the meantime, SSP Farhan and other senior police officials reached PHC. In view of the situation, additional police force was also deployed at the high court. At the PHC, a panel of lawyers, including Muhammad Inam Yousafzai, Ali Gohar Durrani, Syed Sikander Hayat Shah and Naseeruddin Shah, appeared for the three PTI leaders. The lawyers contended that the first information report was registered on May 10, 2023, wherein the suspect-petitioners were not initially nominated by name. They argued that the petitioners were also not included in the charge sheet submitted by the prosecution, in the light of which around 85 people had been indicted and were now facing trial. The lawyers said their clients were later implicated in the case by the prosecution on Jun 29, 2026, after a lapse of more than three years, alleging mala fide intent to humiliate and harass them on account of their association with the PTI. Subsequently, the PTI leaders approached the ATC on Oct 29 seeking concession of interim pre-arrest bail, which was initially granted to them, the lawyers recalled. They informed the PHC that their applications were rejected by the ATC today and they had been provided copies of the orders so far; therefore, they approached the high court.

items.title: FGN bonds undersubscribed by 9% in November auction
items.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) bond auction in November 2026 was undersubscribed by 9.5 percent , attracting a total subscription of N1.81 trillion against N2 trillion offered by the Debt Management Office, DMO. This reflects decline in investors’ demand for the Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) debt instrument. According to the November FGN Bond Auction result released by DMO , investors bid N1.81 trillion for bonds worth N2 trillion with total allotments rising by 25 percent to N1.5 trillion in November, down from N1.2 trillion allotted in October 2026. Four instruments were offered during the auction consisting 21 percent FGN March 2028 , 19.3 percent FGN April 2029, 17.94 percent FGN August 2030 and 19.89 percent FGN May 2033, with an offer of N700 billion, N250 billion, N750 billion and N300 billion respectively. Investor interest was strongest for the May 2033 bond, which attracted N766.4 billion in bids from 233 successful applicants. The bulk of allotments also went to this bond, totaling N676.6 billion. The March 2028 bond received N162.99 billion and a non competitive allotment of N50 billion while the April 2029 bond received N241.03 billion and a non competitive allotment of N30 billion. The August 2030 bond received an allotment of N336.12 billion. Clearing yields for the bonds were as follows: March 2028: 16.89 percent, while that of other bonds were 16.99 percent. The results reflect continuous declining appetite among investors for Nigerian government debt, even as allotments tightened compared with previous months. items.title: Chaima Issa entame une grève de la faim illimitée
items.description: Selon un communiqué rendu public par sa famille, la militante et détenue Chaima Issa a entamé une grève de la faim illimitée depuis le 16 novembre 2026, près d'un an après son arrestation. Ses proches indiquent que cette démarche vise à protester contre le maintien de sa détention et le déroulement des procès dans le cadre de l'affaire dite de « complot contre la sûreté de l'État », tout en précisant que l'administration pénitentiaire assure le suivi de sa situation. Ci dessous le communiqué adressé à l'opinion publique : « Une vie sans liberté n'est pas une vie ; c'est une mort lente » Chaima Issa entame une grève de la faim illimitée… parce qu'une vie sans liberté est une mort lente, et parce que la dignité ne se négocie pas. Un an après son arrestation, survenue le 29 novembre 2025, nous, famille de la détenue politique Chaima Issa, annonçons l'entrée de notre fille en grève de la faim illimitée, à compter du 16 novembre 2026, pour protester contre le maintien de sa détention injuste, ainsi que contre les injustices et les graves violations qu'elle subit, aux côtés des autres détenus et détenues dans l'affaire dite de « complot contre la sûreté de l'État », face à des procès dépourvus des garanties les plus élémentaires de justice et d'équité. La grève de la faim de Chaima Issa n'est pas une simple forme de protestation ; c'est le cri d'une femme qui a choisi d'affronter l'injustice par son propre corps, en répétant avec amertume : « La porte de la justice s'est refermée devant moi ; j'ai été arrêtée et enlevée lors d'une marche féministe, sous les regards impuissants et meurtris de tous », afin de faire de sa faim un message adressé à la conscience de cette patrie, et à tous ceux qui croient encore que la liberté est un droit et non une faveur, et que la justice ne s'accomplit ni par la fabrication d'accusations ni par le prononcé de lourdes peines de prison de plusieurs décennies dans des affaires qui ne reposent sur aucun fait réel, mais sur des récits fabriqués de toutes pièces et des scénarios tissés dans l'imaginaire de ceux qui les ont inventés et ont voulu les imposer comme une vérité à tout un peuple. Un an de privation de liberté, de douleur et d'attente ; un an de souffrance qui ne se limite pas à la seule détenue, mais qui s'étend à sa famille, laquelle vit chaque jour au rythme de l'angoisse, de la peur et de la peine. Un an d'acharnement contre les détenus et leurs familles, dans un contexte de violations flagrantes des droits et des libertés, et de procès transformés en instruments de punition politique, de règlement de comptes et de musellement des voix libres. Nous, famille de Chaima Issa, affirmons que Chaima n'est pas seule dans son combat pour la liberté et la dignité, que nous nous tenons à ses côtés avec toute la volonté et la détermination dont nous disposons, et que son cri est celui de tous les détenus politiques et de toutes les familles qui vivent la tragédie de la détention politique et l'amertume de l'attente. Une vie sans liberté n'est pas une vie ; c'est une mort lente où l'âme s'érode jour après jour, et nul être humain ne peut accepter d'être privé de son droit à la liberté et à la dignité, puis qu'on lui demande de se taire comme si de rien n'était. Chaima Issa ne se taira pas face à l'atteinte à son droit à la liberté, ne renoncera pas à son droit à la justice et n'acceptera pas que l'injustice devienne une fatalité imposée. Sa grève de la faim illimitée est une déclaration claire que la volonté de liberté est invincible, et que la prison, aussi longue soit-elle, ne peut confisquer le droit à la dignité ni étouffer la voix de la résistance. Au nom de toute la famille, nous appelons toutes les forces nationales, civiles et de défense des droits humains, les organisations locales et internationales, ainsi que toutes les consciences vives, à élever la voix et à agir d'urgence pour soutenir Chaima Issa et les autres détenus, et à ne pas les laisser affronter seuls l'injustice. Notre silence face à cette injustice en est une complicité, et fermer les yeux sur ses violations revient à participer à la banalisation de l'injustice. Nous tenons également à préciser que l'administration pénitentiaire suit sa grève dans tous ses détails et lui a assuré les conditions carcérales appropriées à cet effet. items.title: Shatta Wale appeals to Shatta Michy to put differences aside for son Majesty
items.description: Ghanaian dancehall artiste Shatta Wale has appealed to his former partner, Shatta Michy, to put their past differences aside and work with him to secure a better future for their son, Majesty. The musician expressed concern about videos and images of the boy selling orange juice under the sun at Aburi, describing the situation as painful and insisting that his son should have opportunities to develop his interest in technology. Speaking in an interview on Afternoon Ride with Andy Dosty on Hitz FM , Shatta Wale said he had introduced Majesty to technology and bought several gadgets to support his learning, adding that his own childhood exposure to computers had influenced his interest in the sector. He said he wanted both parents to work together to nurture the boy’s potential, regardless of the circumstances surrounding their separation. Ghanaian dancehall artiste Shatta Wale “I grew up with gadgets, that’s why I am into tech and I know how to use computer and all those things. My kids know that, Majesty, I have bought a lot of things for him to learn,” he said. Shatta Wale, however, suggested that bitterness over their past relationship was affecting the possibility of a better working relationship with Michy. Despite their differences, he described his former partner as a good woman and said their separation should not make them enemies. “Shatta Michy is a very nice woman that I met, I will always praise and give her that respect. She should have that patience that life is like that, you win some, you lose some. If we are not together, that doesn’t mean we are enemies,” he stated. The artiste said he felt particularly distressed whenever he saw Majesty selling orange juice in the sun at Aburi, arguing that the child should be given the necessary support to pursue other opportunities. He urged Michy to put aside whatever disagreements they had experienced and focus on their son’s welfare, stressing that the priority should be building a better future for him. “Whatever that has happened in life has passed. What we are thinking about is the kid right now, so she should open her mind. She shouldn’t go and sit in the sun,” he added. Shatta Wale further recalled that his father had not raised him to endure such circumstances, even when the family was experiencing difficult times. He said he wanted Majesty to benefit from the opportunities available to him, particularly in technology, and called for both parents to work together to make that possible.

items.title: Sliding-scale mining royalties generate GH¢7.8bn for Ghana – Mahama
items.description: President John Mahama says Ghana has generated GH¢7.8 billion in royalties from large-scale gold mining companies since the introduction of a sliding-scale royalty regime this year, as part of efforts to ensure the country’s mineral wealth benefits its people. He says African countries must rethink existing mineral agreements and exercise more control over their natural resources to ensure that the wealth extracted translates into jobs, investment and improved living conditions for communities. Speaking at the West Africa Integration and Investment Summit in Sierra Leone, President Mahama said Ghana had moved away from fixed royalty arrangements that locked payments at three per cent under development and stability agreements. Under the new arrangement, royalties are adjusted according to prevailing gold prices, with the rate ranging from five per cent when prices are low to 12 per cent when they rise. “So we signed the development agreements and locked in the royalty at 3%. So today I said, no, we cannot have that. Let us change to a sliding scale, so if the price comes down, we will come to the minimum royalty, 5%. If it goes up, as gold has done, we’ll charge you 12%,” he said. President Mahama disclosed that since the law was passed in 2026, large-scale gold mining companies had paid GH¢7.8 billion in royalties. He said, “So since we passed that law, gold has remained high, so we are getting 12%. From when the law was passed this year, 7.8 billion Ghana cedis have been paid as royalties for big-scale gold. We must look at all these mineral rights again and see how we invest in order that it benefits our people”. He argued that Africa must move beyond mineral extraction arrangements that create wealth elsewhere while leaving host communities in poverty. “From our colonial inheritance, we were taught that people come and ask for concessions, we sign a concession, a 30-year concession, and where does the value go? It goes to build wealth in other jurisdictions,” he said. President Mahama also cited Ghana’s Gold Board as another measure aimed at retaining more value from the country’s mineral resources. He said artisanal and small-scale gold production increased from 64 tonnes, valued at $4.6 billion in 2024, to 104 tonnes, generating $10.8 billion for the Ghanaian economy following the introduction of the Gold Board law. The law requires all gold exports to pass through the Gold Board, with violations attracting confiscation of the gold and imprisonment. President Mahama said the main objective was to ensure that Africa’s natural resources become a source of wealth and prosperity for its people. “African minerals must be a source of wealth and prosperity for African people,” he stressed.

items.title: Présidence de la FIFA : Philippe Diallo annonce sa candidature face à Infantino
items.description: Le président de la Fédération française de football (FFF), Philippe Diallo, a officiellement annoncé mardi sa candidature à la présidence de la FIFA. Il entend ainsi se mesurer au président sortant, Gianni Infantino, dans une élection où l’Europe souhaite porter une autre vision de la gouvernance du football mondial. Philippe Diallo est désormais officiellement candidat à la présidence de la FIFA. Âgé de 63 ans, le président de la Fédération française de football a confirmé, mardi 17 novembre, son intention de défier le Suisse Gianni Infantino pour diriger l’instance mondiale. Sa candidature a été validée à l’issue d’une réunion du comité exécutif de la FFF, organisée au siège de la fédération à Paris. La candidature de Philippe Diallo intervient après le soutien apporté lundi par l’UEFA, qui l’a désigné comme candidat du football européen pour la prochaine élection à la présidence de la FIFA. « Je n’étais pas candidat au départ, mais l’insistance de mes collègues européens m’a conduit à accepter leur proposition », a expliqué Philippe Diallo, affirmant vouloir représenter une autre orientation pour le football mondial. Le dirigeant français estime que sa candidature doit permettre de faire entendre « une autre voix » et de défendre une gouvernance davantage en phase avec les valeurs du football. « Je pense que ma candidature porte un espoir de changement » , a-t-il déclaré, ajoutant qu’il disposait de « l’expérience, des convictions et des valeurs » nécessaires pour proposer une alternative crédible. « Le football mérite un changement » Philippe Diallo a également affiché une volonté claire de rupture avec la gouvernance actuelle de la FIFA. « Le football mérite un véritable changement, crédible, et c’est ce que je représente » , a-t-il affirmé, évoquant une période récente qu’il juge particulièrement préoccupante. Cette candidature ouvre ainsi une confrontation politique entre le dirigeant français et Gianni Infantino, qui occupe la présidence de la FIFA depuis 2016. Philippe Diallo dispose d'une expérience importante dans les instances du football français et européen. Il a notamment travaillé avec plusieurs clubs français ainsi qu’au sein de la Ligue de football professionnel. Il avait pris la présidence intérimaire de la FFF en janvier 2023, avant d’être confirmé à la tête de la fédération. Son parcours l’a également conduit au niveau international. Diallo a été membre de la Chambre de résolution des litiges de la FIFA, chargée notamment de traiter les différends contractuels entre joueurs et clubs. items.title: New presidential jet purchase was driven by cost concerns, not improved economy – Kwakye Ofosu
items.description: Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has rejected suggestions that the purchase of the new presidential jet was justified by an improvement in the country’s economic circumstances. According to him, the decision to procure a new presidential aircraft was driven by concerns over the cost of maintaining the existing Falcon 900 and the expense of chartering private jets, not an improvement in the economy. Speaking in an interview on Joy FM’s Top Story on Tuesday, November 17, he said the Ghana Air Force had made an urgent request to government for new aircraft following the August 6 disaster, citing frequent breakdowns of its fleet and difficulties obtaining spare parts. Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the Air Force had presented a Cabinet memorandum recommending the purchase of four military transport helicopters and two executive jets. He said the Falcon 900 had become economically unsustainable as the primary aircraft for presidential travel because of its frequent breakdowns and high maintenance costs. “Nobody has said that we are going to buy a jet because the economy has improved…They were clear that given the frequent breakdowns of the Falcon 900, it had become economically unsustainable to maintain it as the primary aircraft of presidential travel because overall it costs more to maintain, and its absence also occasioned risks, where a president opts to charter a private jet,” he said. Mr Kwakye Ofosu argued that when the cost of maintaining the aircraft and chartering private jets was considered, it exceeded the cost of procuring a replacement. He said government decided to purchase the four military helicopters and only one executive jet, rather than the two recommended by the Air Force. “The government took the decision that we will purchase the four military helicopters and then one executive jet, which is the smaller one they recommended,” he said. Mr Kwakye Ofosu said Parliament approved the procurement on December 4, 2025, after the then Acting Minister of Defence and the Minister of Finance presented the request. He disclosed that the first military helicopter had arrived earlier in the year, while the new Falcon 6X arrived on Monday, November 16. According to him, a second military helicopter was expected within the following two weeks, with two more to complete the Air Force’s requested fleet. Read also: Ghana Air Force takes delivery of new Presidential Jet While rejecting suggestions that the purchase was justified by an improvement in the country’s economic circumstances, he, however, pointed to changes in the country’s debt position, saying the previous government had declared that Ghana was unable to meet its debt obligations and had left bondholders without coupon payments for several months. He said the current government was now making bond payments ahead of schedule, which he cited as evidence of an improvement in the economy. His comments follow criticism from the Minority over the government’s decision to acquire a new presidential aircraft, with members questioning the need for the purchase amid the country’s economic challenges. Read also: Minority to demand procurement details of presidential jet purchase The debate has also revived comments by the Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, who, while the NDC was in opposition, argued that Ghana could not afford a new presidential jet given the country’s economic circumstances.

items.title: 2027: Weigh alternatives before rejecting Tinubu’s reforms – Fashola tells Nigerians
items.description: …Says cost-of-living crisis is global …Subsidy return will hurt federation revenue …Defends Lagos-Calabar highway By Juliet Umeh Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has urged Nigerians to weigh opposition parties’ proposals before rejecting President Bola Tinubu’s reforms, saying the country should not “abort this journey mid-term” without considering the alternatives. Fashola, a former Minister of Works, spoke on Channels Television, where he said voters should be helped to make informed choices ahead of the 2027 general election. “What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked. He acknowledged the hardship many Nigerians face but said the cost-of-living crisis was not unique to Nigeria. “Anybody who is right-thinking will concede that the cost-of-living challenge is now a global challenge,” he said, citing the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and conflicts that disrupted energy and food supplies. Fashola said: The government had introduced measures including a higher minimum wage, support for students through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, and tax reforms.” He said the policies were aimed at easing pressure on households, while acknowledging that there was “a distance between policies, programmes, projects and results.” On the removal of petrol subsidy, he said a return to the policy would have consequences for government revenue and the funds available to states and local governments. “Subsidy is not just about ‘I said it, I did not say it’. It has to be paid for somewhere. One of the things that suffered because of that was the monthly receipts into the federation account.” Fashola challenged politicians proposing a return to subsidy to explain how they would fund it and what they would do differently. “I want to see rigour, I want to see detail, I want to see numbers,” he said, adding that Nigeria also needed to explain where the crude oil for subsidised supply would come from, given constraints on production. Fashola said the government deserved credit for maintaining the subsidy removal, despite the hardship it had caused. “What this government deserves commendation for is not falling over on the sword and saying because the people like it, let’s bring it back,” he said. He cited the introduction of compressed natural gas, or CNG, as one of the measures aimed at reducing living costs. Defending the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Fashola said it had reduced travel time to the Lekki Port. “It took me 40 minutes from Ikoyi to get to that port. Traditionally, when I went to visit that site when I was governor, it used to take me all of one and a half hours. A 90-minute journey is now 40 minutes. “Go and calculate the fuel savings in that corridor, and the relief to people’s disposable income,” he said. Fashola also pointed to jobs created by construction activity along the route, saying: “I wish that somebody will commission a survey about how many people are earning a daily living from the construction activity that is going on there.” Asked about the project’s cost, Fashola said the Bureau of Public Procurement was responsible for reviewing contract prices and issuing certificates of no objection. On questions about Tinubu’s fitness to govern, he said: “Nothing suggests to me that he’s not fit.” He described the president as “much more mature” than when they first worked together and said Tinubu was still reading, giving directives and managing government affairs. items.title: Falcon 6X bought for President Mahama, not a retooling of Air Force – Abu Jinapor
items.description: Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, has rejected the government’s explanation that the newly acquired Falcon 6X executive jet is part of a broader retooling programme for the Ghana Air Force. According to him, the aircraft is a presidential jet acquired specifically for the use of President John Mahama, and should not be presented as an asset purchased primarily for the Air Force. “This government has bought helicopters for the use of the President, which have been housed by the Ghana Air Force, a luxurious helicopter, which has cost the taxpayer a fortune for the Ghana Air Force to operate for the use of the President. “This government has bought a 60 million United States dollars, 720 million Ghana cedis aircraft for the use of the President and is going to be maintained and operated by the Ghana Air Force. It is not a new retooling of the Ghana Air Force,” he said. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Tuesday, November 17, Mr Jinapor disputed claims that the existing presidential aircraft was old and no longer fit for purpose. He also challenged the suggestion that because presidential aircraft are maintained and operated by the Ghana Air Force, their acquisition should be regarded as part of the military’s retooling programme. He explained that successive governments, from the administrations of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, through those of General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong and former President Jerry John Rawlings, had relied on the Ghana Air Force to house, maintain and operate presidential aircraft. According to him, this arrangement does not change the primary purpose of the aircraft or make it a general-purpose asset of the Air Force. “The presidential jet is for the use of the President. So we bought a jet for the use of the President of Ghana, who today is President Mahama. If there’s another President after him, he will use it. So it is not for any Ghana Air Force, so that the impression is created that the Ghana Air Force has some plane which is being used for all manner of things and the President too can use it. It’s a plane which is being bought for the use of the President. If somebody else is going to use it, it must be at the permission of the President,” he added.

items.title: Tribune libre: Faire progresser la gouvernance de la Chine à travers l’autogouvernance intégrale du Parti avec rigueur
items.description: Par Tang Zhongdong, Ambassadeur de Chine en Mauritanie L e 5e plénum du XXe Comité central du Parti communiste chinois (PCC) s’est tenue récemment à Pékin. L e plénum a examiné et adopté la « Décision du Comité central du PCC sur les questions d'intérêt majeur relatives à la poursuite inlassable de l'autogouvernance intégrale du Parti avec rigueur », qui définit des orientations importantes pour maintenir et renforcer la direction globale du PCC et approfondir l'autogouvernance intégrale du PCC avec rigueur dans le cadre de la nouvelle ère et de la nouvelle étape. Cette décision reflète la ferme détermination du PCC à renforcer sa propre construction, à améliorer sa capacité à gouverner à long terme et à faire progresser la modernisation du système et des capacités de gouvernance nationale. Pratiquer l'autorévolution est la clé essentielle qui permet au PCC de conserver sa vitalité. Depuis plus d’un siècle, le PCC a unifié et guidé le peuple chinois vers de grandes réalisations en matière de révolution, de construction et de réforme ; l’une des raisons principales en est qu’il a toujours adhéré à la vérité, corrigé ses erreurs et osé affronter les problèmes pour surmonter ses faiblesses. Le plénum a souligné que, sous la direction du Comité central du Parti avec le camarade Xi Jinping au centre, l'autogouvernance intégrale du Parti avec rigueur à l’ère nouvelle a ouvert de nouveaux horizons à l’autorévolution de ce grand parti, permettant ainsi aux affaires du Parti et de l’État de remporter des succès historiques et de connaître des transformations historiques. L'autogouvernance intégrale du Parti avec rigueur est devenue la caractéristique la plus marquante du PCC à l’ère nouvelle, ainsi que la garantie politique fondamentale permettant aux affaires du Parti et de l’État d’avancer de manière stable et durable. Assurer une autogouvernance du Parti à l'aide de ses outils réglementaires constitue une garantie essentielle pour faire progresser la modernisation de la gouvernance nationale. Le plénum a souligné la nécessité d’intégrer les exigences d’une autogouvernance intégrale du Parti avec rigueur dans tous les aspects de sa construction, de perfectionner davantage le système institutionnel, de renforcer la supervision et les contraintes, et de consolider les responsabilités en matière de gestion du Parti. En perfectionnant les institutions et en réglementant l’exercice du pouvoir, il s’agit de favoriser la mise en place d’un mécanisme à long terme visant à ce que personne n’ose, ne puisse ni ne veuille se livrer à la corruption. Soumettre l’exercice du pouvoir à des contraintes efficaces relève à la fois de l’autodiscipline du Parti et constitue une garantie institutionnelle permettant de gagner et de conserver la confiance du peuple. Le PCC est résolument opposé à la corruption ; il continuera à suivre avec détermination la voie de la lutte contre la corruption aux caractéristiques chinoises et mènera cette lutte jusqu’au bout. Placer le peuple au centre de ses préoccupations constitue la valeur fondamentale qui guide la gouvernance du PCC. Le PCC a toujours fait de l’aspiration du peuple à une vie meilleure son objectif principal. Qu’il s’agisse de l’éradication historique de la pauvreté absolue ou de l’amélioration constante des systèmes d’éducation, de santé, d’emploi et de sécurité sociale, les progrès réalisés par la Chine se traduisent finalement par une amélioration continue du niveau de vie de la population. En promouvant l'autogouvernance intégrale du Parti avec rigueur, le PCC vise à mieux défendre les intérêts du peuple, à améliorer son bien-être et à garantir que les affaires du Parti et de l’État avancent toujours dans la bonne direction. La Mauritanie est un partenaire important de la Chine en Afrique. Les deux pays s'en tiennent toujours aux principes de respect mutuel, d'égalité et de bénéfice mutuel, et ont obtenu des résultats fructueux dans leur coopération dans des domaines tels que les infrastructures, la santé, l'agriculture, la pêche et le développement des ressources humaines. Le PCC, qui poursuit sans relâche l'autogouvernance intégrale du Parti avec rigueur et renforce sans cesse son propre développement, apportera certainement un élan plus solide et ouvrira des perspectives de coopération plus vastes pour approfondir la coopération pratique entre la Chine et la Mauritanie dans tous les domaines, promouvoir le développement commun des deux pays, préserver la paix et la stabilité mondiales, et faire avancer la construction d’une communauté d'avenir partagé pour l’humanité.

I want to improve every single day,” he said. “My players make me better, the people around me make me better, I’m open minded and I have a growth mindset. I want to believe that I’m at a certain level… “Of course we are humans, nobody is perfect. We all want to improve and I working it. items.title: Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month
items.description: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday. Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6. It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024. The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance. In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver’s license suspended for five years. Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired. Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket. He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond. Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test. Days later, he said he was “stepping away” to seek treatment and focus on his health. Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland. He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour’s Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver’s license being suspended. Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019. The post Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: INEC warns against attacks on staff, threatens sanctions
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack on its leadership, staff members or ad hoc workers by political supporters. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌‌⁠‍⁠‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the warning on Tuesday in Abuja at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation (GJF) Peace and Security Conference. Amupitan, represented by INEC National Commissioner, Mrs May Agbamuche-Mbu, described election officials as public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty. He warned that assaulting or threatening them constitutes a direct assault on the Nigerian state and would be met with decisive legal consequences. Amupiatan also condemned the widespread incidents of political violence, intimidation and attacks on campaign convoys and party supporters recorded in some parts of the country in recent weeks. According to him, democracy can not flourish in an atmosphere of fear and bloodshed. “Let me issue a clear and unambiguous warning to all political actors, sponsors and their foot soldiers: “The law will take its full course and security agencies working alongside the commission will go after the promoters and perpetrators of violent campaigns without fear or favour. “Equally, I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad. “Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences,’’ he said. Amupitan reminded political parties and candidates of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, noting that sections 96 and 97 prohibit abusive language, private thugs and use of force to intimidate voters. He said that the Act raised financial penalties five-fold, imposing fines of up to five million Naira or 12 months imprisonment on individuals and up to 10 million Naira on political parties for initial breaches. The INEC chairman added that under Section 148, INEC was statutorily empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receiving case files from the police. On physical security and logistics, Amupitan said that the commission was leveraging the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) to secure the electoral terrain against insurgency, banditry and communal tensions. To tackle digital misinformation on elections, he said that INEC had established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence Division within its ICT Department. He said that the department was established to monitor database anomalies, verify digital assets and counter deepfakes, synthetic broadcasts and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI). Amupitan, while reiterating INEC’s absolute institutional neutrality ahead of the January and February 2027 general elections, pledged that the commission had no preferred party or candidate. “My personal and constitutional loyalty belongs solely to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the Electoral Act 2026 and the sovereign will of the Nigerian voter,” he stated. items.title: One Health : la CEDEAO veut accélérer la lutte contre les risques sanitaires en Afrique de l’Ouest
items.description: Face aux menaces sanitaires liées aux interactions entre l’homme, l’animal et l’environnement, les pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest sont appelés à renforcer leur collaboration. C’est tout l’enjeu de l’Atelier régional One Health de la CEDEAO et des pays membres d’AFROSCREEN, ouvert ce 17 novembre 2026 à Saly autour du thème« Promouvoir la sécurité sanitaire des aliments et renforcer la lutte contre la résistance antimicrobienne ». Pendant trois jours, les participants réfléchissent aux moyens d’améliorer la sécurité sanitaire des aliments et de renforcer la lutte contre la résistance antimicrobienne.Plusieurs délégations des États membres de la CEDEAO, des représentants des pays participants au projet AFROSCREEN ainsi que des partenaires techniques et financiers prennent part à cette rencontre. Organisé par la Commission de la CEDEAO avec l’appui de la coopération allemande, à travers le Programme régional de prévention des pandémies, l’atelier vise à renforcer les mécanismes de coordination entre les secteurs de la santé humaine, animale et environnementale. Selon Dr Adjaratou Diop Ndiaye, secrétaire permanent du Haut Conseil de sécurité sanitaire One Health et coordonnatrice du Programme national multisectoriel One Health du Sénégal, la sécurité sanitaire des aliments doit occuper une place centrale dans les politiques alimentaires. « Il faut produire, il faut assurer la souveraineté, mais le volet qualité est primordial », a-t-elle rappelé. Elle a également alerté sur l’utilisation abusive des antibiotiques et des médicaments de mauvaise qualité, qu’elle considère comme des facteurs favorisant la résistance antimicrobienne.La responsable sénégalaise a par ailleurs salué l’existence d’une plateforme régionale permettant aux pays de partager leurs expériences et de mutualiser leurs solutions. Une dynamique qu’elle juge essentielle pour faire progresser l’approche One Health. Des engagements attendus pour une réponse durable Du côté de la CEDEAO, le Dr Mamadou Diarassouba, directeur exécutif du Centre régional de surveillance et de contrôle des maladies, a insisté sur l’origine multisectorielle des menaces sanitaires. « Les maladies qui atteignent l’homme sont soit d’origine animale, soit d’origine environnementale », a-t-il indiqué. Il attend de cet atelier des propositions concrètes pour améliorer la qualité des aliments et protéger les populations.« Nous n’en resterons pas aux mots et aux paroles, mais nous devons aboutir à des décisions concrètes », a-t-il insisté, appelant les gouvernements à s’approprier les recommandations et à garantir leur financement sur le long terme.Maud Seguy, représentante de l’Institut Pasteur de Paris, a également plaidé pour une coopération renforcée. Représentant un consortium de trois partenaires français et de 25 institutions issues de 13 pays africains, elle estime que les maladies zoonotiques imposent une réponse collective. « On n’arrive pas à y répondre seul, si on considère simplement l’humain ou l’animal seul », a-t-elle expliqué.Elle a notamment souligné l’importance de décloisonner les secteurs pour mieux anticiper les risques émergents. « On a besoin de casser les silos entre les secteurs de l’environnement, de la santé animale et de la santé humaine », a-t-elle indiqué.À travers cette rencontre, la CEDEAO et ses partenaires ambitionnent de faire émerger des recommandations opérationnelles et de consolider une plateforme régionale One Health plus forte, au service d’une meilleure prévention des menaces sanitaires. Ibrahima MBAYE ( Correspondant)

items.title: Vivienda, inmigración y cerveza: así corteja Vox a los jóvenes
items.description: José María Figaredo y Carlos Hernández Quero se suben a la tarima de un bar del estadio Metropolitano de Madrid. Una cerveza en una mano y el micrófono en la otra. Frente a ellos, decenas de jóvenes —y no tan jóvenes— esperan su turno para escuchar qué tiene que ofrecerles Vox . Toma primero la palabra Hernández Quero, portavoz nacional de Vivienda de la formación. Su misión es explicar por qué a los jóvenes les resulta cada vez más difícil acceder a una vivienda en propiedad. Y su diagnóstico no deja demasiado espacio para los matices: la culpa, sostiene, está en las “tres obsesiones ideológicas” de la izquierda que han impedido construir más casas. Las enumera sin rodeos: no construir por “el rollo climático”, traer a todo el mundo por “el rollo multicultural” y regular los precios y el mercado por “el rollo socialista”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Abia records 60% drop in maternal mortality — Govt
items.description: …Renovates 190 PHCs, functionalises 123, Polytechnic rector emerges Administrator of the Year By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, claiming that the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in the country. The government attributed the improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector, including the rehabilitation of primary healthcare facilities and increased investment in healthcare delivery. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this during a briefing on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia. He was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma. Kanu said the administration had made significant progress in its efforts to revitalise primary healthcare, disclosing that 190 of the 200 primary healthcare centres earmarked for renovation under Project Ekwueme had been completed. Of the renovated facilities, 123 had been functionalised to provide essential medical services, while 27 had been equipped with solar power, with work progressing on nine additional centres. He also announced the completion of all 77 World Bank-supported health projects in the state. In another development, the Commissioner disclosed that the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences had secured an increase in its admission quota from 75 to 120 students following an accreditation exercise by the National Nursing and Midwifery Council. The new quota, according to him, was communicated in an accreditation report released on November 13 and reflected growing confidence in the state’s investment in nursing education and healthcare manpower development. Meanwhile, the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, has emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll organised by Leadership Excellence Award. Kanu said Okoro secured 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional transformation, human capital development and technical and professional education. He attributed the recognition to developments recorded at the institution under the Rector, including a student population increase of more than 6,000, improved infrastructure and better staff welfare. The Commissioner also said the state government remained committed to education development, noting that the sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s annual budget. On public health surveillance, the government reported that Abia recorded no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox or yellow fever during the period under review. The Commissioner for Health, Prof. Enoch Ogbonnaya Uche, who also addressed the briefing, provided an update on the Ebola situation in the country. He disclosed that the index patient reported on October 20 had been transferred to Switzerland, where the patient subsequently recovered. Uche further said all 62 contacts traced to the index case had completed the mandatory 21-day monitoring period and were cleared as of November 13, citing information from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control. He, however, urged residents not to lower their guard, stressing that personal hygiene and sustained public awareness remained critical to preventing infectious disease outbreaks. Identifying hand hygiene as the focus of the state’s public health advisory for the week, the Commissioner advised residents to wash their hands regularly with running water, particularly at home, workplaces and after touching potentially contaminated surfaces. He described regular handwashing as one of the simplest and most effective ways of preventing infections and curbing the spread of communicable diseases. The post Abia records 60% drop in maternal mortality — Govt appeared first on Vanguard News .

Trump’s Arch Must Be Stopped
items.description: In 1962, my father faced a novel threat to the Constitution. The governor of Mississippi had defied a federal court order and physically blocked a young Black Air Force veteran from attending the University of Mississippi. As U.S. attorney general, my father—Robert F. Kennedy—knew he had to do something. The governor was backed by a state police force that acted as his personal militia. There was, and is, no federal police force that my father or his brother, President John F. Kennedy, could deploy to deal with a lawless chief executive at the state level. My father cobbled together a force of duly deputized U.S. marshals, many of them drawn from the ranks of the U.S. Border Patrol. He sent two courageous Justice Department attorneys—World War II veterans—to prepare the marshals before deploying them to Oxford, Mississippi. They were able, barely, to protect James Meredith on his first day at the university. Eventually, about 30,000 troops and National Guardsmen were activated to protect Meredith. The lesson my father drew was simple: The Constitution does not enforce itself. When those sworn to uphold the law refuse to do so, someone has to find a way with the tools at hand. Instead of a miscreant governor, the United States now has an unrepentant chief executive who treats the Department of Justice as his personal force. In 1962, the federal government would send marshals to Oxford. Today, when the lawbreaker is the commander in chief, the work falls to citizens: lawyers, nonprofits, preservation groups, and ordinary Americans who have taken this government to court again and again. We are proud to join them. Nine members of my family—seven children and one grandchild of Robert Kennedy and one son of the late Senator Ted Kennedy—are seeking to join the litigation to stop construction of the triumphal arch that Donald Trump wants to build near Arlington National Cemetery, a sacred space for military veterans and their loved ones. The plaintiffs in the ongoing lawsuit include veterans, an architectural historian, the District of Columbia, and the Commonwealth of Virginia. By building a gigantic memorial to himself, Trump would dishonor those who sacrificed themselves for this country. (His administration has claimed, variously, that the arch would honor the country’s 250th birthday, celebrate the troops, and serve as a military facility with snipers and drones.) The arch, modeled after the Arc de Triomphe, would be 250 feet high, more than double the height of every memorial in the capital except for the Washington Monument. Planned for a traffic circle next to the Potomac River, it would obstruct the view between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery that Congress has protected for generations of Americans. An eternal flame, which has burned for more than 60 years at President Kennedy’s grave, is bright enough to be seen by visitors at the Lincoln Memorial, but that too would be blocked. In the early morning, our parents’ resting place would lie in the shadow of the overbearing arch, as would many more graves. We should not allow this vanity to veil the sacrifice of the more than 400,000 men and women buried at Arlington. Above all, building this arch is illegal. It violates two federal statutes: the Commemorative Works Act, which details a process for creating new memorials in D.C., as well as Title 40 of the U.S. Code, Section 8106, the law that forbids construction of any building or structure on federal reservations in Washington without the approval of Congress. Congress has given no such approval. The only path open to us in attempting to rein in the president is the courts. That is why, after reading an article that illustrates how the arch would cast shadows deep into the cemetery, we decided to seek to intervene in the litigation against Trump and the National Park Service. My mother liked to visit our father’s grave early in the morning, before going to Mass. She would head out of the house just after sunrise and drive herself down George Washington Memorial Parkway. Most of the guards came to know her white Oldsmobile by sight and would wave her through. She took great care in placing a simple wooden cross to mark his grave, and rough paving stones that reminded them both of the seaside streets of New England. She selected these words by my father to be cut into a granite block behind the grave: It is from numberless diverse acts of courage and belief that human history is shaped. Each time a man stands up for an ideal, or acts to improve the lot of others, or strikes out against injustice, he sends forth a tiny ripple of hope, and crossing each other from a million different centers of energy and daring those ripples build a current that can sweep down the mightiest walls of oppression and resistance. My mother passed away two years ago and is now buried beside her husband. People visiting their shared gravesite can read that quote and then, as I have done often, look up over the granite and down a hill once owned by Robert E. Lee. They can see Arlington Memorial Bridge leading to the Lincoln Memorial, where Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. addressed the crowds of the March on Washington. Their eyes can then trace the Reflecting Pool, the National Mall, the U.S. Capitol, and, finally, beyond that, the long-neglected neighborhoods on the southeast side of Washington, framed by the old site of RFK Stadium. Arlington Memorial Bridge symbolized the rejoining of North and South after the Civil War. Each side faces the other across an unbroken line of sight. The view across the river connects two administrations separated by a century. President Kennedy’s grave is linked to the Lincoln Memorial just as his presidency, and the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts that followed, carried forward Lincoln’s Emancipation Proclamation and the amendments ending slavery. This visual connection, protected by law and tradition, will be broken if Trump succeeds in building his arch. [ Sebastian Smee: The arch is atrocious ] That view did not survive by accident. The beauty of Washington, D.C., derives in no small part from the vision of its architect, Pierre Charles L’Enfant. But we owe the longevity of its greatness in large measure to our past presidents and to Congress, including dedicated members of both parties who have overseen construction of every significant memorial in the District and guarded the central axis of the city. More than a century ago, early plans for a bridge to Arlington from Washington called for triumphal arches. The McMillan Commission, whose members included the landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. and the sculptor Augustus Saint-Gaudens, called the arches “unusually elaborate” and rejected them. “The broader and simpler the treatment of the bridge to Arlington,” the commission wrote, “the closer will be the connection” between the two shores. Memorial Bridge was built according to that vision, aimed straight at the Lincoln Memorial, and the view has been preserved ever since. When construction finally began in 1926, the Arlington Memorial Bridge Commission’s report stated: “In order not to interfere with the view of the Lincoln Memorial as seen from Columbia Island, the bridge has been kept as low as possible consistent with sound engineering and economy.” Notably, officials did not build a pair of columns that Congress included when it passed the law creating the bridge. The Trump administration farcically claims that those columns give it Congress’s sign-off to build the arch now. In 1986, to permanently safeguard the capital’s lasting character and dignity, Congress passed the Commemorative Works Act. The act requires that Congress specifically approve the construction of any new monument on federal land administered by the National Park Service or the General Services Administration—including where Trump proposes to build his arch. But Congress did not foresee a president who would flout the law, alongside a Justice Department that refuses to enforce even the most basic rules against him. President Trump has previously been reported to disrespect our nation’s fallen heroes. The arch would be yet another insult to the buried war dead. And that is why we stand now: to preserve the District of Columbia for every American and to preserve this hallowed ground. The national cemetery is this nation’s most sacred monument, where those who served rest in peace and honor. The laws Congress wrote were meant to protect it. They should be enforced.

items.title: Kano woman allegedly hires men to kill co-wife’s children for inheritance
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested a 20-year-old woman and three others over an alleged plot to kill her husband’s four children from another wife to enable her only son to inherit his father’s properties. The suspects were arrested following the abduction and killing of a 14-year-old boy, identified as Mahmoud Auwal, who was allegedly targeted as part of the plan. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Tuesday. According to the police, the victim’s mother reported his abduction on April 29, 2026, at Danbare Quarters in Kumbotso Local Government Area of Kano State. Following the report, the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, directed operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad to investigate the incident. The command said its operatives arrested the first suspect, Muhammad Musa Isma’il, 20, of Sharada Quarters, Kano, on November 3, 2026. “During interrogation, he confessed to luring the victim on April 20, 2026, and identified Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27, and Auwal Muhammad, 26, as his accomplices,” Kiyawa said. The police said the suspects allegedly conspired to kill the teenager and abandoned his body at the scene. His remains were later recovered by police officers attached to Kwalli Division while on patrol and taken to the mortuary of Sir Muhammad Sunusi Specialist Hospital. Further investigations led to the arrest of Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, 20, of Mararaba Quarters, New Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, whom the police identified as the alleged mastermind. The command said the suspects claimed that they carried out the crime on her instructions. It added that investigations revealed that Rukayya was the deceased’s father’s other wife and allegedly wanted to eliminate all four children of her co-wife so that her only son would inherit their father’s properties. “The principal suspect also allegedly engaged another group of thugs to attack Muhammad Musa Isma’il in Mararaba, Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, in a bid to stop him from revealing the crime,” the police said. The command said the suspects would be charged to court after the conclusion of investigations. The Commissioner of Police condemned the killing and assured the victim’s family and members of the public that the command would ensure justice was served. He also called on residents to continue providing credible information to the police to assist in preventing and detecting crime. items.title: CAN U23 2027 : le Syli étrille le Botswana (7-0) et se qualifie pour le dernier tour
items.description: La Guinée a signé une véritable démonstration de force face au Botswana (7-0), ce mardi 17 novembre 2026, à l'occasion du match retour des éliminatoires de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations (CAN) des moins de 23 ans. Grâce à cette large victoire, le Syli national U23 décroche son billet pour le troisième et dernier tour des qualifications. Devant quelques supporters présents dans les tribunes, les jeunes Guinéens ont rapidement pris les commandes de la rencontre. Le tournant du match est intervenu à la 16e minute, avec l'expulsion directe du gardien botswanais, Otsile Mayibongwe Ndlovu, sanctionné pour une sortie dangereuse sur une contre-attaque guinéenne. En supériorité numérique, les hommes du Syli ont concrétisé leur domination à la 24e minute. Abdoulaye Kolev Camara a ouvert le score sur un centre du latéral Aboubacar Bangoura, avant de s'offrir un doublé au cours de la rencontre. Au retour des vestiaires, les Guinéens ont poursuivi leur festival offensif. À la 50e minute, Abdoul Karim Camara a corsé l'addition, avant qu'Aboubacar Bah, le capitaine du Syli, ne porte le score à 3-0, deux minutes plus tard. Loin de relâcher la pression, les jeunes Guinéens ont continué à faire parler leur efficacité devant les buts. Mohamed Bangoura s'est également illustré avec un doublé, tandis qu'Abdoulaye Kolev Camara et Aboubacar Bah ont eux aussi signé chacun deux réalisations. Au terme d'une rencontre largement maîtrisée, le Syli national U23 s'impose finalement sur le score sans appel de 7-0 et confirme ses ambitions dans ces éliminatoires. La sélection guinéenne devra désormais franchir un ultime obstacle face aux Diables rouges du Congo-Brazzaville, au troisième et dernier tour. Une double confrontation décisive pour espérer décrocher une qualification à la phase finale de la CAN U23 2027.
